entries.controlling_text: Specification status: Controlling implementation and acceptance specification

Execution model: Application-native deterministic execution wherever the proposition can be faithfully represented; otherwise exact routing to an independent AI reviewer, capable external tool, human inspection, or external system
Primary objective: Maximize the probability that the final delivered product is actually correct while preventing unsupported confidence and minimizing opportunities for human or AI error.
1. Inspect the actual repository and establish the true current starting commit.
3. Preserve every working mechanism that satisfies this specification.
4. Correct every repository behavior that conflicts with this specification.
5. Implement the smallest complete changes necessary.
6. Test the application through the visible live user interface as a human operator would use it.
8. Test every affected downstream path after every upstream correction.
9. Preserve every reproduced defect as a permanent regression.
12. Use the deployed application through the real operator path before claiming completion.
1. Return an audit as a substitute for implementation.
2. Return a patch archive, downloadable bundle, replacement project, or instructions for the user to install manually as a substitute for modifying the actual application.
3. Stop after editing only Stage 01, Stage 04, or another isolated portion.
4. Declare success because source code looks correct.
5. Declare success because syntax tests pass.
6. Declare success because unit tests pass.
8. Declare success before replaying the exact failed user path in the live application.
10. Perform cleanup, refactoring, renaming, architecture modernization, or style changes that are not required to correct a demonstrated defect.
11. Rewrite working systems merely because another design is possible.
12. Create parallel stores, engines, parsers, prompt systems, shells, or workflow implementations.
13. Ask the user to repeat information the application already possesses.
14. Make the user manually allocate identifiers, calculate hashes, construct schemas, connect routine relationships, calculate gates, or retype canonical information.
15. Place instructions intended for external agents anywhere except the exact generated prompts controlled by prompt-engine.js.
Automated tests are mandatory, but they are not a substitute for live operator-path verification.

One observable failure → identify the earliest responsible layer → apply one minimal complete correction → replay the exact visible path → verify affected downstream behavior → preserve the failure as a regression.
Section 0 directs only the implementation agent modifying and verifying the repository.
Its instructions are not runtime project requirements, external-stage instructions, canonical project data, operator content, or prompt content.

The application MUST NOT copy, paraphrase, display, store, export, or delegate Section 0 or other user-to-implementation-agent instructions into project records, operator screens, generated prompts, execution packages, schemas, or delivered artifacts unless a separate substantive product requirement expressly requires the same runtime behavior. prompt-engine.js contains only instructions needed by the external actor for the current project stage and operation.
The controlling disposition for every gate, stage determination, release determination, and terminal determination is evaluated in this exact order:
1.1 Any current sufficient refutation of an applicable mandatory proposition -> REJECTED.
1.2 Otherwise any required unknown, insufficiency, contradiction, stale state, unresolved blocker, or unavailable mandatory capability -> BLOCKED.
1.3 Otherwise every applicable mandatory proposition satisfied -> ACCEPTED.
1.4 All blockers and contradictions remain recorded even when REJECTED controls the disposition.
- The authoritative external prompt is a file, not clipboard contents or a rendered preview.
- The authoritative external response is an ingested JSON file, not pasted text.

- A stage obligation is not due before its defined target exists and its EARLIEST_EXECUTABLE_STAGE has been reached.
- Authorization to deliver is not evidence that delivery occurred.
- Implementation instructions are not runtime agent instructions.
The controlling normative source is the exact UTF-8 file `specification/closed-loop-reliability-controlling-implementation-specification.txt` in the exact audited source commit.

CI MUST generate `specification/closed-loop-specification-manifest.json` as a repository-only closed-loop-specification-manifest/1 after reading those exact bytes and MUST generate `specification/closed-loop-normative-requirements.json` as the corresponding normative-requirement manifest.

That manifest records the source commit, repository path, artifact filename, byte length, SHA-256, section inventory, contract-profile identity, and the identity and digest of the normative-requirement manifest.
The manifest and source commit together identify the exact specification used for implementation and acceptance; the specification does not contain a self-referential digest of itself.
The controlling runtime contract profile is closed-loop-completion-profile/1.
Runtime project state, prompts, responses, packages, imports, exports, and receipts carry only the contract profile and the particular schema or registry identities required for their own operation.

The specification text, its repository-only manifest, Section 0 implementation instructions, user-to-implementation-agent instructions, audits, and repair commentary are not runtime project data and MUST NOT be embedded in the application, generated prompts, execution packages, canonical records, or operator screens merely to establish conformance.
A closed-loop-project/3 object that lacks the current contract profile is legacy /3 data.
It MUST be deterministically migrated with complete migration receipts or preserved as historical and non-gating.
Schema-name equality alone does not establish current contract conformance.
Repository governance MUST maintain one machine-readable closed-loop-normative-requirements/1 manifest generated from and reviewed against the controlling specification.

It assigns a stable NORMATIVE_REQUIREMENT_ID to every distinct normative requirement, prohibition, invariant, field contract, operation contract, negative case, regression obligation, deployment obligation, and definition-of-done metric.

Each entry records the controlling text location, responsible implementation owner, schema or registry entry, deterministic and semantic test IDs, mutation-test IDs, required browser or physical-device proof, acceptance-report field, and current disposition.
This manifest is implementation and acceptance evidence outside runtime project state.
It MUST NOT be injected into ordinary project prompts or carried by the application as project content.
CI rejects missing, duplicated, untraced, or conflicting normative entries and rejects an acceptance claim when any current mandatory entry lacks the required implementation and proof relationships.
Manifest completeness is established under the same omission-challenge discipline this specification imposes on project content.

One extractor drafts the manifest from the controlling text; an independent reviewer that did not receive the draft performs its own extraction or section-by-section coverage pass; a distinct reconciliation resolves every difference; and every specification section is either covered by entries or explicitly recorded as nonnormative with a reason.
CI records the challenge and reconciliation evidence with the manifest digest.
An unreconciled material disagreement, an uncovered section, or a missing challenge record blocks acceptance.
For every external-agent operation, the application exports the exact authoritative prompt as a UTF-8 text file and exports any required manifest and input artifacts as files.
The external agent returns one authoritative UTF-8 JSON response file plus any declared returned artifacts.
The application ingests those file bytes directly.
Clipboard copy, pasted JSON, and large text-entry transport are optional nonauthoritative conveniences only and cannot be required for completion.
The required physical mobile operator path is the pinned actual-iPhone Safari acceptance target defined in Section 45.
Browser-neutral desktop verification remains required where specified.

The prompt uses accepted requirements and tests.

Visible explanation: The application is proving every mandatory requirement has a complete evidence chain.

Completion: Every mandatory chain is structurally complete, current-scope, evidence-sufficient, and linked to current artifact identity where applicable.
Stage 30 — PRESERVE FAILURES PERMANENTLY AND CLOSE DELIVERY

Completion: Defect and regression histories are append-only; corrections are new records; every confirmed defect has a permanent regression; every due applicable regression execution is current; the pre-delivery checkpoint exists;
CALCULATE_TERMINAL atomically creates one AUTHORIZED or BLOCKED delivery determination under Section 36.9.
Export or share and any delivery completion are separately receipted and never inferred from authorization.

Stage 30 closes through the one atomic CALCULATE_TERMINAL command, which reads the precondition revision, validates registry integrity and all terminal prerequisites, creates exactly one current terminal determination, sets DELIVERY_STATE = AUTHORIZED only when every prerequisite is true and otherwise BLOCKED, increments revision once, and commits once.
The command's own committed revision does not invalidate its result; only a later revision affecting its dependency closure may supersede or withdraw it.
Registry incompleteness blocks Stage 30 unless it proves an earlier premise false; it does not create a Stage 27↔Stage 30 cycle.
